requirement: Build a modular, reliable URL shortener from the supplied scaffold, not merely a hardening patch. Preserve POST /api/v1/urls (201 {code,shortPath}), GET /{code} (302 Location, no-store), and GET /api/v1/urls/{code}/analytics (200 {code,clicks}). Support generated 12-character URL-safe codes, bounded collision retries, custom aliases with reserved-name validation, absolute HTTP(S) URL validation, optional future expiration, inactive/expired/unknown 404, atomic successful redirect click counts, duplicate alias 409. Implement separate controller, service, repositories, validation/policy, configuration and metrics components. PostgreSQL is authoritative; preserve V1 migration and add a new migration for durable Idempotency-Key handling: same payload replays same response, changed payload conflicts, concurrent requests cannot create duplicates, retention configurable. Use Redis cache with bounded TTL and expiry correctness, database fallback on Redis failure, atomic Redis rate limiting with expiry for create and redirect, 429 on exhaustion, explicit fail-open policy with metrics on Redis failure, and no trust of forwarded IP headers by default. Use parameterized SQL, bounded connection timeouts, no committed secrets, and health/Prometheus metrics. Include complete Maven configuration and new Flyway migration where necessary. Add independent unit tests and real PostgreSQL/Redis Testcontainers integration tests executed by Maven verify (Failsafe for *IT), covering API contracts, idempotency, collisions, expiration, analytics, cache and rate limiting/failure. Preserve existing regression tests. Design must enumerate exact production and new test file paths and shared interfaces; do not defer any required capability or replace real integration tests with mocks. Human approval precedes generation and external verification must use actual Maven evidence.
